newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bourse rally after Spain budget may be minimal.
newsitem.headline: Bourse rally after Spain budget may be minimal.

text.p: Madrid stocks may have gained all the benefit they can from the forthcoming 1997 budget, especially if the accounts are not as strict as some equities analysts anticipate.

The market has soared in anticipation of a stringent budget that will allow the Bank of Spain to cut its key interest rate from 7.25 percent and will whip Spain into shape for the common currency launch.
Many are still expecting the measures, which should be announced on Friday, to get Spain on track for monetary union in 1999, consequently boosting stocks and bonds.

But others believe the bourse's upside potential is limited, either because the government will not manage to come up with sufficiently austere measures, or because those same measures have already been factored into share prices.
"A restrictive budget has already been discounted. I don't think stocks will take off because of the budget," an equities research director at a Madrid brokerage said on Wednesday.
"The net effect on the bourse will probably be positive, but not as much as people are estimating," he added.

The five-month-old conservative government has pledged to deliver a stringent budget that will slash the deficit to three percent of gross domestic product in 1997 from a projected 4.4 percent this year.

To do so, the government is counting on revenue growth of six percent, while it contains spending growth at two percent. Even so, it must still slash 800 billion pesetas ($6.3 billion) in expenditure.
But the research director was sceptical of just how restrictive the budget might be.
"The budget may yet be surprising, with the (government) backing off from what they've said they'll do."
The Ibex-35 index of leading stocks has risen from 3,932.40 at the close on July 30 to 4,135.72 at close of trade on Tuesday. But some say the end may be in sight.

Mariano Colmenar, equities research director at BZW in Madrid, said "I'm a little sceptical really. We've already seen a tremendous gain in the bond markets. My gut feeling is that really should be corrected."
The brokerage sees the bourse general index at 380 points by the end of the year, but believes the markets' advance immediately after the budget could be limited.

But other brokers see the budget providing yet more fuel for stocks, and expect prices to make good progress towards 400 points on the General Index and 4,400 on the Ibex-35 index of leading stocks, where many see the bourse by year-end.
Societe Generale, for example, sees the general index hitting around 380 within a month after the budget.
"(The budget) should create confidence in the economy and pave the way for rate cuts, which will support the stock market," an analyst there said.
Among sectors, construction stocks are among the worst hit in advance of the budget details.
They are already discounting sharp cuts in infrastructure spending, analysts say. The government has said it plans to reduce public investment by 100 to 150 billion pesetas next

Shares have been factoring in expected lower income growth next year since the government has indicated it would have lower tariff increases in the price-regulated sector, which makes up the bulk of the market.

But this could be partly offset by the fact that Spain's risk premium will fall as bond markets are likely to take the budget well, with yields falling as a consequence. -- Madrid newsroom +341 585 2160 ($1=127.3 Peseta)
